title: Sequential coalition formation and the core in the presence of externalities
abstract: The sequential coalition formation model of Bloch to solve cooperative games with externalities exhibits some anomalies when related to classical concepts. We elaborate on these problems, define a modification of Bloch's model and show that its order-independent equilibria coincide with the (pessimistic) recursive core.
summary_en: Bloch's classical sequential coalition-formation model is widely used to solve cooperative games with externalities, but Kóczy shows it produces anomalies when applied to standard solution concepts. He proposes a modification of Bloch's model and proves that its order-independent equilibria coincide with the pessimistic recursive core — a non-cooperative foundation for the recursive-core concept. The result bridges cooperative and non-cooperative game theory in settings with externalities, useful for applications ranging from international treaty design to industrial alliances.
data_used: Theoretical model — sequential coalition-formation games with externalities. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Provides a non-cooperative microfoundation for recursive-core analysis used in evaluating Hungarian and EU coalition-formation problems: EU enlargement bargaining, Visegrad cooperation, energy-supply coalitions. Useful for any policy analysis where the order in which coalitions form matters and externalities exist between them.
